title: Forty by noon
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. Forty copies in the rack at nine. Gone by noon. Not to a church bus. To the town, one at a time. The owner says he should print more. He says forty's the number. She says the number's changed. He prints forty.

panels.composition: Nine AM. The rack, full: forty. WOOD setting the last in. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young man setting the last of forty small booklets into a wire rack in a laundromat at morning, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Noon. The rack: the realtor's flyer, the bulletin, the digest's slot empty.

image.prompt: close on a wire rack at midday with its booklet slot empty between a flyer and a bulletin, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Forty's the number I can carry.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner speaking to a young man by an empty rack, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood walking to the Datsun with the empty box the copies came in. Forty. Next Friday, forty. The strip has a ceiling and it's his arms.

image.prompt: a young man carrying an empty cardboard box to a small car outside a laundromat, a small dog trotting beside, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Forty's the number I can carry.' The ceiling is his arms.
